purpose: Dallas final asset-library completeness and Gamecast determinism QA: prove every active-roster identity resolves only to its own approved appearance/action inventory, survives production cache/version transitions, and fails safely without contaminating live event truth.

qualityContract.appearanceAuthority: current official headshot lock only; never infer visible appearance from player name
qualityContract.identityAuthority: DAL/roster.json player slug plus current uniform number
qualityContract.fallback: Any identity, version, decode, action or provenance failure disables only the affected personalized layer and preserves authoritative Gamecast presentation.

qaChecks.assert: Exactly 53 active Dallas roster entries map one-to-one to 53 personalized player namespaces; duplicate slugs, numbers or cross-player aliases fail release.
Every personalized namespace resolves to that player's own official-headshot-derived appearance lock; unresolved provenance blocks personalization rather than guessing.
Every action requested by Gamecast must be explicitly authorized for that player in roster.json; physical archetype supersets never grant runtime eligibility.
A scene may not mix incompatible personalized asset manifest versions for the same player; version transitions occur at a safe play boundary or fall back.
Cache keys include team, player slug, action and immutable asset version so stale or colliding content cannot substitute another player/action.
Base/action/signature frames preserve clean transparent alpha with no opaque matte, clipped extremity or detached shadow artifact.
Action and recovery transitions preserve canonical foot anchor and scale without visible teleport, cumulative drift or viewport-dependent identity shift.
Current Dallas uniform number remains readable and unmirrored whenever visible; a number mismatch is a hard personalized-render failure.
At most one authoritative football is visible and ownership follows accepted play truth across pass, catch, rush, fumble, recovery, kick and correction transitions.
Only the verified Lamb nose-wipe first-down and Miller DeSoto Shuffle sack sequences may use named Dallas signature routing; no other named signature is invented.
Polling, rerender, resize, reconnect and cache hydration cannot reconsume an action or signature for an already-consumed authoritative revision.
Dallas QA/runtime namespaces cannot mutate MLB or NHL assets, caches, stores, routes or presentation behavior.

acceptanceFixtures.assert: Roster/namespace audit returns exactly 53 unique active Dallas players and no orphan personalized namespace.
An intentionally colliding player/action filename cannot cross-resolve because team/player/version cache identity remains distinct.
Asset manifest version change during a live play keeps the accepted scene coherent until a safe boundary, then loads the new version or falls back.
A personalized frame carrying a stale/wrong uniform number is rejected without altering authoritative Gamecast content.
Missing appearance provenance suppresses personalization for that player and never substitutes inferred or teammate appearance.
A position-archetype action absent from the player's roster.json inventory is rejected even when a physical asset exists.
Idle-to-action-to-contact-to-recovery chain returns to canonical foot anchor within authored tolerance with no accumulated drift.
Pass-to-catch-to-fumble-to-recovery plus an authoritative correction never displays two footballs or stale ownership.
An authoritative CeeDee Lamb first down may consume nose-wipe once; identical polls and cache hydration cannot replay it.
An authoritative Von Miller sack may consume DeSoto Shuffle once; correction removing the sack preempts it immediately.
Any unverified named Dallas celebration request resolves to generic eligible celebration or no celebration, never a fabricated signature.
Executing the full qa-05 fixture set causes zero writes to MLB or NHL files/state and requires no MLB/NHL behavior change.
